 OMODA & Jaecoo face pressure to ensure quality after a series of incidents in Southeast Asia.
 Incidents involving wheel systems on some OMODA & Jaecoo (Cherry-owned) models in Southeast Asia are putting the leading Chinese automaker under pressure to further demonstrate its quality control capabilities as it expands globally.
 Hà Nội Mới • 07/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The vehicle was involved in an accident in Malaysia in October. Photo: PV The focus of the concerns began in Malaysia, where an OMODA 5 suffered a serious accident on October 6th in Johor Bahru. While in transit, the rear axle assembly and suspension system unexpectedly detached from the vehicle's body. Images of the SUV with its entire rear axle assembly missing quickly spread on social media, raising questions about structural integrity and the manufacturer's quality control processes.
 The Malaysian authorities reacted quite strongly. On October 11, the Malaysian Road Transport Department (JPJ) temporarily suspended the Vehicle Type Approval (VTA) for the OMODA 5, meaning new registrations for this model were halted while the investigation continued. The agency also requested Chery to cooperate in reviewing the manufacturing and assembly processes, inspecting welds, and checking the quality of wheel axle components.
 On October 14th, Chery Malaysia announced a recall program for 8,878 OMODA 5 vehicles across both C and H variants. Affected vehicles will undergo a comprehensive inspection and component replacement if necessary, completely free of charge. Notably, the figure of 8,878 represents the total number of vehicles included in the inspection campaign and does not mean all vehicles will be found to have the defect. 
 An OMODA vehicle during a test drive in Vietnam. Photo: Hoang Linh Under pressure from the incident, Chery Chairman Yin Tongyue publicly apologized to Malaysia. Speaking at the World Conference on Intelligent Connected Vehicles (WICV) on October 21, he said he had met directly with the Malaysian Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry to apologize for the product quality issues, and emphasized that Chery does not seek short-term profits abroad but aims to build a long-term presence in international markets.
 This is not the first time OMODA 5 has encountered problems related to the rear axle in Malaysia. In 2024, Chery conducted a preventative inspection campaign on 600 vehicles after a similar incident. Chery explained at the time that the cause was due to the welding equipment being incorrectly calibrated after replacing the welding head, resulting in substandard weld quality.
 Notably, while the controversies in Malaysia were still ongoing, another incident involving the Jaecoo brand occurred in Indonesia . On November 4th, a Jaecoo J5 EV was involved in an accident on KH Mas Mansyur Road, Karet Tengsin area, Tanah Abang district, central Jakarta. Footage recorded by passersby shows the electric SUV lying motionless on the median strip, with the right front wheel assembly and suspension components detached from the vehicle. Part of the front bumper and related parts were also scattered on the road.
 You may also like Initially, some reports in Indonesia suggested the rear wheel had detached from the vehicle. However, Jaecoo later confirmed the damage was located at the front right corner. According to the technical inspection results released by Jaecoo Indonesia, the vehicle collided with a curb and concrete median before the wheel assembly detached. The company stated that this was a consequence of the collision, not the cause of the accident, and affirmed that no signs of product defect were detected.
 Nevertheless, the timing of the Jaecoo J5 EV incident inevitably brings controversy, especially since the Jaecoo J5 EV is currently the best-selling all-electric passenger car in the Indonesian market.
 A more significant development occurred on November 6th, when the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of China announced a recall campaign for 53,882 Chery Tiggo 5x and OMODA models in the domestic market. According to notice code S2026M0146V, the recalled vehicles were manufactured between June 6, 2022, and December 31, 2023. The cause was identified as a welding process issue at the connection point between the rear axle's longitudinal control arm and the bushing. Under harsh operating conditions, the weld is at risk of breaking, affecting rear wheel control and increasing the risk of accidents.
 A series of adverse events poses a significant challenge to Chery's internationalization strategy. In recent years, the group has boosted exports and expanded its presence in many markets, particularly in Southeast Asia, where demand for SUVs, electric vehicles , and hybrids is rapidly increasing. Incidents related to structural safety, regardless of their specific causes, can impact consumer confidence in the brand. 
 OMODA & Jaecoo need to make efforts to ensure vehicle quality as the brand seeks to penetrate the Vietnamese market more deeply. Photo: Hoang Linh In the automotive industry, a product can attract customers with its design, features, technology, or competitive price. But to maintain a long-term position, manufacturers must demonstrate reliability throughout the product's lifespan.
 Chairman Yin Tongyue's apology shows that Chery has recognized the pressure from the incidents in overseas markets. However, what customers and regulators need is not just commitments, but also transparent investigation results, thorough corrective measures, and verifiable quality control mechanisms.
 Chery needs to conduct a comprehensive review of all relevant component assemblies, particularly the axles, hubs, suspension system, and high-load connection points. If similar risks are found in other models using the same platform or components, the company should proactively implement preventative measures.
 You may also like In particular, Chery should strengthen its collaboration with independent testing agencies in each market. Involving third parties in assessing the cause, confirming corrective measures, and checking the quality after repair will increase objectivity and reduce potential doubts that may arise when the manufacturer makes its own conclusions about its products.
 Chery also needs to invest more heavily in its local technical infrastructure, from service staff training and diagnostic capabilities to parts inventory and claims handling procedures. When problems arise, customers need quick access to information and clear inspection and repair plans.
 Overall, for Chery in general and OMODA & Jaecoo in particular, the current challenge lies not in responding to individual incidents, but in demonstrating the quality control capabilities of the entire production and supply chain system, thereby proving the competence of a global automotive manufacturer. Overcoming the current problems will also provide an opportunity to transform the quality challenge into a foundation for OMODA and Jaecoo's ambitious development in Southeast Asia.
